target_customer: Software engineers wanting an AI-native, privacy-first IDE
problem: Engineers wanted AI agents that work across many files in the codebase rather than single-file autocomplete.
business_model: Open-source (AGPL-3.0) editor with planned commercial offering; no revenue found

founders.name: Sandeep Pani
founders.background_notes: Open-source contributor to gRPC and Bazel per YC description; ACM ICPC world finalist (YC long description, team of two).

founders.name: Naresh Ramesh
prior_employers: Payments company (infrastructure for 150k merchants in India)
founders.background_notes: Scaled an engineering team from 5 to 35 per YC page.

exit.reason: Repository archived and no longer maintained; one secondary article says they could not compete with the funding and speed of Cursor, Windsurf and CLI agents (not verified against the founders' own X post).

technical_complexity.rationale: Building agents with language-server, sandboxed terminal and semantic code-graph tooling on a VS Code fork was hard for two people; they claimed 43% on SWE-Bench Lite.

defensibility.rationale: Open-source AGPL fork of VS Code with no data or network moat; easily replicated by better funded teams.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: By Feb 2025 the team stopped, per a secondary article citing inability to compete with Cursor, Windsurf and vendor CLI agents.

market_need_then: Strong developer demand for AI coding assistants in 2023; the YC launch page shows slow onboarding via Discord and Twitter but no user counts.

branding.domain_note: aide.dev for the product; company name CodeStory is a separate brand

identity.voice_and_tone: Engineer-to-engineer, open-source community voice (YC launch posts)

branding.community_and_virality: GitHub repo reached about 2.2k stars and 341 forks before archive.

brand_strength.rationale: Product name Aide was distinct from company name CodeStory; no press on the brand and no origin story found.

pivots.to: Aide, a VS Code fork IDE
pivots.why: YC launch described an extension; later product was a fork (not stated why).

outcome_analysis: CodeStory built Aide, an open-source AI IDE, in London after YC S23 and gained 2.2k GitHub stars. The repo was archived on 25 Feb 2025 and the project declared unmaintained. A single secondary source attributes the stop to being unable to match the funding and speed of Cursor, Windsurf and vendor CLIs, which is plausible but not confirmed by the founders. No institutional funding was found beyond the YC deal.
notes: Funding: CB Insights lists a 0.5M convertible note (unverified aggregator, consistent with the YC deal); no round recorded. The shutdown reason comes from one secondary article; the founders' X announcement was not read. One search result claimed the repo was still maintained in 2026; the GitHub page shows archived Feb 2025. No dated 2023 competitor sources found (searches returned 2026 comparison posts), so list left empty; Cursor and Copilot clearly existed. Name origin for Aide not found. YC lists the company inactive, consistent. Update: the CB Insights convertible note (500K, 2023-01, YC) is now recorded as stage other and rests on a single database; Seedtable dates a 500K seed to 2023-08 and VCBacked a pre-seed to 2023-09, so dates conflict.
